positive.reasoning: Criterion A1 (traumatic event): MET — patient described an event where they felt in grave danger, indicating a traumatic experience. Criterion B1 (re-experiencing): MET — patient reports recalling details of the event unexpectedly and experiencing overwhelming memories. Criterion B2 (avoidance of thoughts): MET — patient actively avoids places and conversations that remind them of the event. Criterion B3 (avoidance of reminders): MET — patient avoids social situations and activities that trigger memories. Criterion C1 (inability to recall details): MET — patient struggles to remember specific details of the event. Criterion C2 (negative beliefs): MET — patient expresses a negative shift in perspective and thoughts about the world. Criterion C3 (blame): NOT MET — patient acknowledges feelings of blame but states they are not constant. Criterion C4 (negative emotions): MET — patient reports consistent negative feelings such as fear and heightened alertness. Criterion C5 (diminished interest): MET — patient shows decreased interest in previously enjoyable activities. Criterion C6 (detachment): MET — patient feels detached from others and prefers solitude. Criterion C7 (inability to experience positive emotions): MET — patient finds it difficult to experience joy or satisfaction. Criterion C8 (irritability): MET — patient reports increased irritability and outbursts. Criterion C9 (recklessness): MET — patient engages in reckless behavior without considering consequences. Criterion D1 (hypervigilance): MET — patient describes increased alertness and difficulty relaxing. Criterion D2 (startle response): MET — patient reports heightened startle response. Criterion D3 (concentration difficulties): MET — patient experiences difficulty concentrating. Criterion D4 (sleep disturbances): MET — patient has trouble sleeping. Criterion E (duration): MET — symptoms began after the traumatic event and have persisted for more than one month. Criterion F (functional impairment): MET — patient reports significant distress and interference with work and social interactions. Criterion G (exclusion): MET — patient denies substance use or medical conditions that could explain symptoms. Total: 14 of 20 criteria met (threshold ≥ 1). Diagnosis: TRUE — full criteria for PTSD are met with significant functional impairment confirmed.
